bytes.accounting: Activation/intermediate traffic counts down BF16 store/read, residual read, layer-output BF16 store/read, next-normalized BF16 store/two quantizer reads, E4M3 store, and one FP32 scale. Both norm weights are reported separately and unchanged.

decision: Promote only row_owned_two_phase_finalizer to an unfunded exact-consumer H200 component contract. Close the epilogue-partial and cluster/DSM families as dominated within this boundary. Do not claim a bench until separately admitted and funded.

decompositions.detail: The 84 stock hidden-tile CTAs can emit exact aligned 64-leaf sum-of-squares partials after BF16 rounding, and the oracle proves they compose to the registered 8192-leaf tree. They do not remove the compulsory down BF16 store/read, add 672 global bytes per row, add epilogue square/reduction work, and still require the same row finalizer. The selected no-partial finalizer saves 672 more bytes per row and avoids the producer modification.
decompositions.extra_flops: At least one BF16-to-FP32 square per down output plus 63 FP32 adds per row/tile.
decompositions.register_shared_risk: Adds epilogue live values to the tuned CUTLASS producer; compiler resources unknown until H200.
decompositions.synchronization: One later kernel boundary; no cross-CTA barrier in the producer.

decompositions.detail: An eight-CTA portable cluster covers only 512 of 5376 columns, so 11 clusters own one row. DSM and cluster barriers do not cross those clusters. Retaining exact row values therefore still needs global materialization and a finalizer, where it is dominated by the selected path. Serializing all 84 tiles through one cluster needs 11 tile slots per CTA and replaces a 0.636-wave producer grid with an 11-slot critical chain.
decompositions.synchronization: At least one global phase boundary or a cooperative-grid barrier; the latter is not the pinned CUDA-graph/CUTLASS launch.

decompositions.cuda_graph: Fixed shape, address, grid, block, and dynamic shared size; capture/replay remains a required target check.
decompositions.detail: Keep the tuned stock down GEMM and its BF16 output. One 256-thread CTA per row uses a 32-KiB FP32 reduction tree plus a 10.5-KiB BF16 row buffer to execute both exact-order RMSNorms, persist only the required next-layer residual, and emit the complete E4M3/scale for unchanged QKV.
decompositions.register_shared_risk: 43,520 dynamic shared bytes; loop-carried scalar registers only by construction. Compiled registers and spills remain an H200 gate.
decompositions.synchronization: One kernel boundary after down; three ordered in-CTA reduction phases and no inter-CTA dependency.

evidence_classes.kernel_totals: measured on the older exact v0.5.13 c32 residual profile; shapes were M=118/1409/1631/2048, not the M<=32 target
evidence_classes.traffic_waves_resources: analytical from pinned source geometry and H200 inventory

reference_oracle.result: All required BF16 residual, registered next-normalized BF16, FP32 scale, complete E4M3, partial-tree, and sampled Q/K/V consumer fragments are bitwise exact for random, signed-zero, and extreme fixtures at M=1/16/32.
reference_oracle.transfer_limit: The oracle proves BF16 boundaries, deterministic reduction decomposition, complete E4M3 bytes/scales, zero/saturation behavior, and sampled first-consumer indexing. It does not prove the pinned Triton reduction order, CUTLASS FP8FastAccum order, compiled resource use, or H200 latency.

source_trace.exact_order: The down result is BF16-rounded before post-FF RMSNorm. The residual/scalar result is BF16-rounded before the next RMSNorm. The next normalized value is BF16-rounded before max/448 scaling and E4M3 conversion.
sequence: Gemma4DecoderLayer gemma_rmsnorm_residual_scalar: BF16 post-FF RMSNorm(down), BF16 residual add, FP32 layer scalar, BF16 layer output
Fp8LinearMethod/apply_fp8_linear/per_token_quant_fp8_small_batch_kernel: BF16 -> row-major E4M3 plus FP32 [M,1] scale
qkv_proj/fp8_scaled_mm: row-major E4M3 [M,5376] x column-major E4M3 [5376,16384] -> BF16 [M,16384]
source_trace.small_batch_zero_semantics: For M<=32 the pinned small-batch quantizer divides by zero on an all-zero row; fmin/fmax converts NaN to +448 and stores FP32 scale +0. The candidate intentionally preserves those bytes.
source_trace.tp_ownership: The qualified endpoint is TP=1. RowParallelLinear would require completion of its tensor-parallel reduction before either row norm at TP>1; the candidate therefore fail-closes to stock for TP!=1.

all_dynamic_quant.kernel: void per_token_quant_fp8_small_batch_kernel<__nv_bfloat16, __nv_fp8_e4m3, (int)16>(const T1 *, T2 *, float *, long, long)

qkv_dynamic_quant.evidence: measured interleaved projection stream, qkv is index 0 of each four-launch layer group

telemetry.shape_transfer_warning: Measured totals came from the older residual profile's prefill-dominant M=118/1409/1631/2048 stream. They bound relevance but do not predict M=1/16/32 latency.

whole_request_bound.interpretation: This is a loose source/telemetry ceiling, not a candidate prediction: the finalizer retains both reductions, residual math, quantization, and all GEMMs. It only establishes that the boundary is positive and stackable enough for a cheap component measurement.
